title: Estimator accuracy and resource bounds
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $S\subseteq J$, and write $W_f(J,S)$ for the sum of squared Fourier coefficients at frequencies formed by adjoining to $S$ any subset of coordinates outside $J$. For real $\varepsilon,\delta>0$, there are rationals $\varepsilon',\delta'\in(0,\tfrac12]$, each strictly between half of the minimum of its corresponding parameter and $\tfrac12$, such that the scheduled estimator with parameters $\varepsilon',\delta'$ has probability at most $\delta$ of error at least $\varepsilon$. Moreover, writing $F=\lceil\log_2\lceil4/\min\{\delta,\tfrac12\}\rceil\rceil$, its failure-bit count is at most $F$, its sample count is at most $16F/\min\{\varepsilon,\tfrac12\}^2$, and every outcome in the support has query cost at most $32F/\min\{\varepsilon,\tfrac12\}^2$ and work cost at most $256F(n+1)/\min\{\varepsilon,\tfrac12\}^2$.
hypotheses_covered: The target is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a subset of the coordinates and $S$ is a subset of $J$
$\varepsilon'$ and $\delta'$ are positive rationals at most $1/2$, each greater than half the minimum of its corresponding real parameter and $1/2$, and each less than that minimum
